title: Atman: Meaning and Context
excerpt: Atman is the Sanskrit word for the self in Hindu philosophy, especially the self that is not merely the body or the social role.

quick_answer.question: What does Atman mean?
quick_answer.answer: Atman means the self. In Vedanta it is often distinguished from the personality, and in Advaita it is taught as not different from brahman.

intro: Atman names the self a tradition says is more than the body, the roles, and the stream of thoughts.

sections.heading: What does Atman mean?
sections.content:
Advaita teachers use atman for the reality that ignorance misreads as a separate person. Other Vedanta teachers use it for a self that remains related to God. The English word soul is only a rough gloss and imports Christian pictures the texts may not share.

The neighboring page is [Atman and Brahman](/articles/atman-vs-brahman/). Treat that link as part of the argument, not as decoration.

sections.heading: Where does the word come from?
sections.content:
The Upanishads and their commentators made the word technical. Britannica's atman article is a short public map. The pair with brahman is the Vedantic habit, not a feature of every Indian school.

A wider map lives at the [Vedanta topic](/topics/vedanta/). Dates and school names matter, because a recent American presentation is often described as if it had no date.

sections.heading: How is the word misused?
sections.content:
When a class says you are not your thoughts, ask whether the next sentence identifies atman with brahman. That next sentence is Advaita. Write it down as a doctrine, not as a lab note.

If you want a narrower practical or comparative page, use [the brahman entry](/glossary/brahman/). You can understand the description without joining a group or buying a course.

sections.heading: What should a careful reader refuse?
sections.content:
Do not use atman to mean self-esteem. Do not use it to dismiss the body as unimportant in ethics or medicine. The word is a philosophical term with rival definitions.

Readers in the United States often meet a simpler version of the same idea in a class, an app, or a short video. Name that simpler version instead of pretending it is the whole tradition. Traditional teaching, personal report, and research stay in separate sentences on this site. The [editorial policy](/editorial-policy/) is the rule. The [disclaimer](/disclaimer/) applies whenever a sentence leans toward health, safety, or a promised transformation. The [corrections](/corrections/) page is how to challenge a factual mistake. Name the school, the text, or the century whenever a sentence would otherwise float free of history. A reader may stop at the definition when that is all the question required.

key_takeaways: Atman is a traditional term with a narrower meaning than popular English often allows.
Schools and modern classes do not all use it the same way.
The glossary states the limit. Longer pages carry the argument.

faq.question: Is Atman a scientific term?
faq.answer: No. It is a philosophical and religious term. Neuroscience does not use it as a measurement.

faq.question: Where is the longer page?
faq.answer: Read the comparison article and the Vedanta explainer.
